History of Present Illness:
47-year-old man. Twelve hours of severe constant epigastric pain radiating to the back and repeated vomiting after several days of heavy alcohol intake.

Physical Examination:
Epigastric tenderness, mild distension and reduced bowel sounds; no focal right lower-quadrant findings. Temperature 37.4 C; heart rate 88/min; BP 116/70 mmHg; respiratory rate 18/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 11.8 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.1 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 220 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 136 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.7 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 45 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 740 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 28 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 25 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 85 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
CT abdomen: diffuse pancreatic enlargement with peripancreatic fat stranding and preserved enhancement. No organized collection.
